analysis.title: Third Quarter 2026 Market Commentary
key_insights: S&P 500 returned +2.3% in Q3 2026 (three months ended 9/30). Russell 1000 Value returned +2.6% and Russell 1000 Growth +0.9%.
Russell 2000 fell 7.2% in the quarter as higher borrowing costs weighed on smaller balance sheets.
MSCI Emerging Markets fell 0.4%. South Korean and Taiwanese equities pulled back sharply after an AI-driven surge in the first half of 2026.
Non-U.S. markets underperformed on a strong U.S. dollar and tighter financial conditions.
The FOMC voted unanimously in September to raise rates 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%, the first hike since 2023, describing the move as having 'removed a dose of accommodation.'
Markets price an additional 100 bps of tightening through end of 2027. The implied December 2027 policy rate rose to 4.8% at quarter-end from 3.89% at the start of the quarter.
10-year and 30-year Treasury yields ended the quarter at 5.27% and 5.62%. The 83 bp rise in the 10-year is among the largest quarterly increases in 40 years.
NEPC attributes the yield move almost entirely to real rates, not higher long-term inflation expectations, which it says remain anchored.
Bloomberg U.S. Treasury Index lost 3.0% and Bloomberg Long Treasury Index lost 8.0% in the quarter.
The France-Germany 10-year spread widened to 124 bps, the widest since the Eurozone sovereign debt crisis, which NEPC reads as fiscal stress.

Spot WTI crude rose above $100 per barrel (+28.1% in the quarter) on escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict. Diesel crack spreads hit record highs on limited global refining capacity, and U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserves are at 40-year lows.
NEPC recommends rebalancing to strategic targets, adding safe-haven exposure, fully using the portfolio risk budget, and keeping a U.S. equity overweight within public equity.

sector_views.rationale: NEPC cites the supportive macro backdrop and broad-based earnings strength unique to the U.S. market.

earnings_insights: NEPC describes U.S. corporate earnings as strong and broad-based, and cites them as a reason to keep a U.S. equity overweight. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The FOMC raised rates 25 bps unanimously, the first hike since 2023.
Markets price about 100 bps of additional tightening through end of 2027.
Up 83 bps in the quarter, driven by real rates rather than inflation expectations.
Long-end yields rose across the curve, producing a large duration loss.
Widest since the Eurozone sovereign debt crisis, signalling fiscal stress.
Supply tightness from the U.S.-Iran conflict, with record diesel cracks and depleted reserves.

risk_factors: Further Fed tightening: markets price about 100 bps more through end of 2027.
Duration losses from continued rises in real yields.
Persistent U.S.-Iran conflict and depleted energy reserves.
European sovereign fiscal stress, shown by the France-Germany spread.
A strong U.S. dollar and tighter financial conditions weighing on non-U.S. markets.
Higher borrowing costs pressuring small caps.
vol_and_positioning: NEPC recommends investors fully use their portfolio risk budget and rebalance to strategic targets.
geopolitical: U.S.-Iran conflict escalated in the Middle East during Q3 and drove energy market volatility.
U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserves are at 40-year lows, raising supply risk if tensions persist.
Fiscal stress in France is reflected in the spread over German Bunds.
